name: HomePod mini (US)

matter.note: Apple lists HomePod mini as a home hub for Matter accessories. CSA's HomePod software listing (Matter 1.0, October 2022) is a software component and names no HomePod model, so a per-model certificate is not confirmed.

apple_home.note: Setting up a HomePod mini makes it a home hub automatically; it adds remote access and automations for HomeKit and Matter accessories, and acts as a Thread hub.

google_home.note: No official source shows HomePod mini-paired devices in Google Home.

alexa.note: No official source shows HomePod mini-paired devices in Alexa.

smartthings.note: No official source shows HomePod mini-paired devices in SmartThings.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's Thread page lists HomePod mini as a Thread border router; it does not say devices paired in Apple Home appear in Home Assistant.

localControl.note: Not confirmed from an official source.

deviceProtocols.note: Apple says HomeKit- or Matter-enabled Thread accessories connect through a Thread-enabled home hub such as HomePod mini.

threadBorderRouter.note: Apple names HomePod mini as a Thread-enabled home hub, alongside third-party Thread border routers; Home Assistant's Thread page lists it as a border router.

maxDevices.note: No limit found in the sources.

summary: Set up a HomePod mini and it becomes an Apple Home hub automatically, adding remote access and automations for HomeKit and Matter accessories. Apple calls it a Thread-enabled home hub, and Home Assistant lists it as a Thread border router. It has Wi-Fi 802.11n and Bluetooth 5.0. Nothing official shows its devices in Google Home, Alexa or SmartThings.

sources.title: Set up your HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV as a home hub
Pair and manage your Matter accessories

caveats: A home hub is needed for remote access and for Thread accessories; the setup page says only home owners can add one to the Home app.
